transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… I’ve been having trouble with driving over high bridges. I plan my days around avoiding them, and if I can’t, I just kind of grip the wheel and get through it.
Is your anxiety about being in a situation where you might see a high bridge, or is it specifically about driving over the bridge itself?
It’s more the actual driving over it. I know those bay bridges are built fine, people use them every day… but when I’m getting near one, my head just goes to the car going over the side.
Do you experience anxiety or discomfort in other situations that involve heights, such as being on the top floor of a building or near a cliff?
Not really sure. I mean, I don’t go looking for cliffs or anything. I haven’t noticed it much in buildings… it’s mainly the bridge thing.
Do you experience anxiety when you are a passenger on a bridge, rather than driving?
Yeah… even just seeing the bridge coming up, I get tense. My chest tightens, hands get sweaty, and I kind of just stare straight ahead until we’re across.
Are you anxious when you're a passenger in other high places, like a tall building or a plane?
I don’t really know. Planes don’t come up much for me, and tall buildings… I can’t say I’ve noticed the same thing. It’s mostly when there’s a bridge involved.
Are you anxious when you are walking on a bridge, not driving or being a passenger in a vehicle?
I don’t really walk on bridges much. But yeah, if I see one coming up, I tense up pretty quick… chest gets tight, hands sweat, and I just kind of stare ahead and want to get to the other side.
Is your anxiety about the bridge itself or the fact that it's high above the water?
It’s more the height over the water, I think. I know those bay bridges are built fine and people drive them every day… but when I get near one, my mind goes to the car going over the side.
Do you experience anxiety when you are in other high places, like a cliff or a mountain, even if there is no bridge involved?
I’m not really sure. I don’t spend much time around cliffs or mountains, so I haven’t noticed it the same way. It’s mostly the bridges that stand out to me.
Is your anxiety about driving over bridges worse when you are driving yourself, compared to when you are a passenger?
Yeah… it’s worse when I’m the one driving. I try to plan my day so I don’t have to go over those high bridges. If I can’t avoid it, I just kind of grip the wheel and get through it.
Is your anxiety about bridges the same when you're driving versus when you're walking or being a passenger?
It’s mostly when I’m driving. As a passenger it’s still not great, but driving is the one I plan around… and if I can’t avoid it, I just grip the wheel and get through.
Do you think your anxiety would be just as bad if you were driving over a high bridge in a simulator, where you knew you were safe?

I don’t know… maybe not as bad if I knew it wasn’t real. But the thing is, with those bay bridges, I know they’re built fine and people drive them every day. Still, when I get close, my mind goes right to the car going over the side.
Would your anxiety about being in high places, like on a bridge, be less if someone else was in control, such as on a train?

Maybe a little less, yeah. If I’m not the one controlling it, it’s not quite the same. But with those high bridges over the bay… I still know they’re safe, people go over them all day, and my head still goes to, you know, what if it goes over the side.
Would you feel anxious if you were on a train crossing a high bridge?
Yeah… probably some. I mean, I know those bridges are built fine and people cross them all day, but when I’m near one, my mind still goes to it going over the side.
Would your anxiety be less if you were on a bus crossing a high bridge?
Maybe a little, if I’m not driving. But… I still know those bridges over the bay are built solid and people cross them all the time. My mind still goes to the vehicle going over the side.
Would your anxiety be the same if you were riding a bike over a high bridge?
Yeah… I think that’d be worse, honestly. I know those bridges are built fine and people go over them every day, but being on a bike up there… my mind would still go to going over the side.
Would your anxiety be the same if you were walking over a high bridge?
Yeah… walking would probably bother me too. I know those bay bridges are solid and people use them every day, but when I’m near one, my head still goes to going over the side.
Would your anxiety about crossing a high bridge be the same if you were on a boat going under the bridge?

Probably not the same. Under it on a boat, I think I’d be less worried… it’s more when I’m up on the bridge. I know they’re built fine and people cross them all day, but when I get near one, my mind goes to the car going over the side.
Would your anxiety be the same if you were crossing the bridge on foot as it is when you are driving?

It’d be pretty close, I think. I know those bridges over the bay are built fine and people drive them every day, but when I get near one, my mind goes to the car going over the side. Walking might feel different, but it’s still the height, I guess.
Is your anxiety about crossing a high bridge limited to when you are driving or does it also occur when you are crossing in other ways?

It’s mostly when I’m up there crossing it, not just the driving part. I mean, I know the bay bridges are solid and people use them all the time, but once I’m near one, my mind goes to… like the car could go over the side.
